name: Computer Science Orientation Seminar
description: A short first-year seminar that introduces the computer science major: degree requirements, career paths, student organizations, and what professional programmers do. Usually pass/fail or low credit, with little or no programming.

name: First-Year Engineering Design
description: Introductory engineering courses taken by all first-year engineering students. They cover the design process, teamwork, problem solving, technical communication, and computing tools such as spreadsheets, MATLAB or Python, and CAD, usually through hands-on team projects.
notes: Often a two-semester sequence, and sometimes split into a design course and a tools course in the same term (as at UC). Every part maps here, so credits add up per school.

name: First-Year Composition
description: A first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision. Students write for different audiences and purposes and learn to find and cite sources.

name: Calculus I
description: Limits, continuity, derivatives and their applications (rates of change, optimization), and an introduction to integrals and the fundamental theorem of calculus. Taught for science and engineering students.

name: Calculus II
description: Techniques and applications of integration, sequences and series (including power and Taylor series), and often an introduction to vectors or parametric and polar curves.

name: Laboratory Science Elective
description: Science courses with a lab chosen from an approved list, typically calculus-based physics, general chemistry, or biology for science and engineering majors. Some programs require a two-course sequence in one science.
first_seen: University of Cincinnati / Science sequence I (PHYS/CHEM/BIOL lecture + lab)
notes: Programs that require one specific science (e.g. physics only) still map here, with the choice recorded in notes. Every semester of the science requirement maps here.

name: Introduction to Programming (CS1)
description: A first programming course for computer science majors. It covers variables, control flow, functions, arrays, basic object-oriented programming, problem solving, and simple algorithms in a language such as Python, Java, or C++.
notes: Some schools spread this over two courses; the second one often maps to data-structures or gets its own canonical course.

name: Co-op Professional Development
description: Short courses that prepare students for co-op or internship work terms and help them reflect on those experiences afterward, covering job search, workplace skills, and career planning.
notes: Specific to co-op programs. Excluded from comparisons with 4-year programs unless a school requires something similar.

name: Computer Organization and Assembly Language
description: How a computer works at the machine level: binary data representation and arithmetic, processor registers, memory, the instruction set, assembly language programming, addressing modes, and input/output.
notes: Some schools combine this with C programming in a systems course, or cover it in a computer architecture course instead.

name: Python Programming
description: Programming in Python as a second language after the intro sequence, including Python's main data types and idioms and common libraries for tasks such as data handling or machine learning.
notes: May be broadened to an additional-programming-language concept during the phase 2 pilot if other schools require a different second language.

name: Data Structures
description: Implementation and analysis of lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs. Covers abstract data types, dynamic memory, recursion, sorting and searching, and an introduction to big-O analysis.
notes: At many schools this is CS2, the second course of the intro sequence.

name: Information Security
description: An introduction to protecting information and computer systems: threats and vulnerabilities, risk assessment, access control, cryptography basics, security policy, and incident response.
notes: UC's course is an introductory IT course with technical and administrative content. Upper-level technical computer security courses may need their own canonical course.

name: Linear Algebra
description: Systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces and subspaces, bases and dimension, linear transformations, determinants, orthogonality, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

name: Discrete Mathematics
description: Mathematical foundations for computer science: logic, proof techniques including induction, sets, relations, functions, counting, and graph theory.
notes: Taught by the CS department at some schools and by the math department at others.

name: Programming Languages
description: Concepts behind the design and implementation of programming languages: syntax and semantics, types, scope, and control and data abstraction, with an introduction to the functional and logic programming paradigms.

name: Intermediate Composition
description: A second-level writing course that builds on first-year composition, with more advanced research, analysis, and rhetorical writing for different audiences and genres.

name: Probability and Statistics
description: A calculus-based introduction to probability (random variables and common discrete and continuous distributions) and statistics (sampling, estimation, and hypothesis testing).

name: General Education Elective
description: Courses outside the major chosen from the institution's general education lists, commonly in the arts and humanities and the social and behavioral sciences.
first_seen: University of Cincinnati / General Education course
notes: UC does not assign gen-ed categories to specific terms, so all of UC's gen-ed slots map here. If schools are later compared by category, this may be split (e.g. humanities vs. social science).

name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Designing and analyzing algorithms: asymptotic analysis, recurrences, correctness proofs, divide and conquer, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.

name: Database Systems
description: Designing and using databases: entity-relationship modeling, the relational model, SQL, normalization, and an introduction to storage, transactions, concurrency, and recovery.

name: Software Engineering
description: Methods for building large software systems in teams: software lifecycle models, requirements, design, testing, maintenance, and professional ethics, usually with a team project.

name: Artificial Intelligence
description: Core ideas of artificial intelligence: problem solving as search, heuristics, game playing, knowledge representation and reasoning, reasoning under uncertainty, and an introduction to machine learning.

name: Operating Systems
description: How operating systems manage processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, memory and virtual memory, file systems, and I/O, often with systems programming assignments.

name: Computer Networks
description: How computer networks work: the layered protocol model, transport and routing protocols, the Internet architecture, and network programming.

name: Technical Writing
description: Professional writing for technical fields, such as reports, proposals, instructions, and presentations, with attention to audience, document design, and clarity.

name: Theory of Computation
description: Formal models of computation: finite automata and regular languages, context-free grammars and pushdown automata, Turing machines, decidability, and an introduction to complexity theory.

name: Senior Capstone Design
description: A culminating project course in which students, usually in teams, specify, design, build, and present a substantial software or computing system that draws on the whole curriculum.
notes: Lasts one or two semesters depending on the school. Every semester maps here, so total capstone credits can be compared.

name: Computer Science Elective
description: Upper-level computer science courses chosen by the student from a department-approved list.
notes: Slot rows may cover several courses (UC lists 6 and 9 credits as single rows), so compare these slots by credits, not row counts.

name: Technical Elective
description: Electives chosen from an approved list that can include computer science courses and supporting technical fields such as mathematics, science, or engineering.
notes: UC calls these directed electives.

name: Co-op Work Term
description: A semester of full-time paid work in the field, arranged through a cooperative education program, with learning objectives and evaluations but no academic credit hours.
notes: Specific to co-op programs and has no normalized semester. Excluded from 4-year comparisons.

name: First-Year Orientation Seminar
description: A short first-year course that introduces new students to the university or college: academic policies, campus resources, study strategies, and an overview of majors and careers. Usually 0-1 credit and often pass/fail.
notes: Broader than cs-orientation, which introduces the CS major itself. Added in step 10.

name: Senior Professional Seminar
description: A short course in the final year about careers after graduation and the transition to professional life. It may include program assessment, such as an exit exam or survey. Usually 0-1 credit.
notes: Added in step 10.

name: Calculus III (Multivariable)
description: Calculus of several variables: vectors and geometry of space, partial derivatives, optimization, multiple integrals, and vector calculus (line and surface integrals, Green's and Stokes' theorems).
notes: Some schools fold part of this into a second-semester engineering math course (e.g. OSU MATH 1172). Added in step 10.

name: Programming II
description: A second programming course that builds on the first: data abstraction, modular and object-oriented design, recursion, and simple linked data structures, with larger programs. Often called CS2 or Software Development.
notes: Sits between intro-programming and data-structures. Some schools cover this material in their data structures course. Added in step 10.

name: Introduction to Proofs
description: A mathematics course on reading and writing proofs: logic, proof techniques including induction and contradiction, sets, functions, and some number theory. A bridge to upper-level mathematics.
notes: Overlaps with discrete-math. Kept separate because it is taught by mathematics as a proofs course, not as discrete structures for computing. Added in step 10.

name: Digital Logic Design
description: Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational circuits (adders, multiplexers, decoders), sequential circuits (flip-flops, registers, counters, finite state machines), and basic hardware design.
notes: Some schools combine digital logic with basic CPU design (e.g. UIC CS 362). Added in step 10.

name: Electronic Circuits
description: Analysis and design of basic electrical and electronic circuits: voltage, current, resistance, circuit laws, and components such as capacitors, diodes, and transistors, often applied to embedded systems.
notes: Added in step 10.

name: Ethics and Professional Issues in Computing
description: Social, ethical, legal, and professional issues in computing: privacy, intellectual property, security, the social impact of technology, and professional responsibility, often through case studies.
notes: Added in step 10.

name: Programming Tools and Practices
description: A practical programming course on the tools and habits of working programmers: debugging, testing, build tools, version control, standard libraries, and advanced language features.
notes: Added in step 10.

name: Team Software Development Project
description: A project course in which student teams design, build, test, and document a sizable software system, such as a web application, an interactive system, or system software, with emphasis on design and written documentation.
first_seen: The Ohio State University / CSE 390X (CSE 3901 or CSE 3902 or CSE 3903)
notes: A mid-program project course, separate from the senior capstone. Added in step 10.

name: Math or Science Elective
description: An additional mathematics, statistics, or natural science course chosen from a list approved by the program.
first_seen: The Ohio State University / Math or Science Elective
notes: Distinct from lab-science (a laboratory science sequence). Added in step 10.

name: Free Elective
description: Any course the student chooses that counts toward the degree, inside or outside the major.
first_seen: University of Illinois Chicago / Free Elective
notes: Added in step 10.

name: Computer Graphics
description: Algorithms and mathematics for producing images and animation by computer: geometric transformations, rendering and shading, modeling, and animation of objects and characters, often applied to interactive applications and games.
first_seen: The Ohio State University / CSE 35X1 (CSE 3521 or CSE 3541)

name: American Government
description: A survey of the government of the United States: the Constitution, federalism, Congress, the presidency, courts, parties, and elections, sometimes with the student's state government. Some states require it of every public-university graduate.
first_seen: The University of Texas at Austin / GOV 310L
notes: Texas requires two courses (UT's GOV 310L and 312L both map here).

name: Differential Equations
description: Ordinary differential equations and their solution methods: first-order equations, linear second-order equations, systems of equations, and applications such as growth, oscillation, and circuits.
first_seen: Texas A&M University / MATH 251 or MATH 308 or STAT 212 (Engineering Mathematics III)
notes: Sometimes combined with linear algebra in one course (e.g. Berkeley's MATH 54).

name: Oral Communication Requirement
description: A course on speaking to an audience, chosen from a list such as public speaking, professional or technical presentation, persuasion, or performance.
first_seen: Texas A&M University / COMM 203 or COMM 205 or ENGL 210 (Public Speaking)

name: Experiential Learning Requirement
description: A required learning experience outside the classroom, such as an internship, undergraduate research, study abroad, or service, usually recorded on the transcript for no credit.

name: Foundations of Data Science
description: An introduction to the mathematics and computation behind data science and machine learning: linear algebra, probability, and working with data in a language such as Python.

name: Technology and Society Requirement
description: A course chosen from a list on how computing and technology affect society, such as technology ethics, the law and policy of data, or the history and sociology of technology.
first_seen: Northeastern University / Computing and Social Issues
notes: Different from computing-ethics, which is one named course in the major.

name: Signals and Systems
description: Mathematical tools for signals and linear systems: signal representation, linear time-invariant systems, frequency analysis, and introductions to feedback control and optimization, usually grounded in linear algebra.
first_seen: University of California, Berkeley / ELENG 66 or ELENG 64 (Introduction to Signals, Dynamics, and Information)

name: Numerical Methods
description: Computing with real numbers on a computer: floating-point arithmetic and error, solving linear and nonlinear equations, interpolation and approximation, numerical integration, and numerical solution of differential equations, with programming exercises.

name: World Language Requirement
description: Study of a language other than English, to a stated level (often the third or fourth semester), or the same proficiency shown by placement or high school study.
first_seen: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Language Other Than English (3rd level)
notes: Credits vary with prior study; a plan places only the courses a typical student takes.

name: Functional Programming
description: A programming course based on the functional model of computation: recursion over inductive data types, higher-order functions, types and type inference, and proofs of program correctness by structural induction, usually in a language such as ML, OCaml, Haskell, or Scheme.
notes: Distinct from programming-languages, which surveys language concepts and paradigms; this is a course in programming in the functional style, often early in the major.

name: Computational Problem Solving
description: A course on general problem-solving strategies for computing: heuristics for mathematical and word problems, generating and evaluating solutions to open-ended problems, solving problems through computation, and problem solving in teams.
first_seen: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University / CS 2104
notes: Not a programming course; a methods course that sits between intro programming and discrete mathematics.

name: Applied Combinatorics and Graph Theory
description: A mathematics course in combinatorics beyond a first discrete math course: counting methods, recurrences, generating functions, and graph theory and graph algorithms.
notes: Split from discrete-math: a second course after discrete math, usually taught by mathematics.
